correctness.rationale: Expanding the squared distance gives Z=d cos t+sin t cos s. The phase shift in t conditional on s leaves a uniform angle; its conditional density is arcsine with amplitude sqrt(d²+cos²s). This proves absolute continuity (the zero amplitude at d=0 occurs on a null set), symmetry and normalization. The integrated denominator is sqrt(A−sin²s), A=1+d²−z². For A>1 factor out sqrt(A); for 0<A<1 the supported angular interval truncates at arcsin sqrt(A), and sin s=sqrt(A) sin u gives K(A). Endpoints give K(0)=π/2. With h=|d²−z²|, the elliptic parameter gap is h or h/(1+h), so both branches give π⁻² log(16/h)+O(h log(1/h)). This yields all sharp constants and a uniform O(d² log(1/d)) remainder on the specified compact λ sets. The monotone square-root distance transform has Jacobian r, gives endpoints M_d±1, and at d=0 gives the small-distance probability r²/(2π). Direct averaging gives E[Z]=0 and E[Z²]=d²/2+1/4, confirming the two moments and identifiability. Independent CDF quadrature plus central differencing matched eight density probes to 1.7e−22 at working precision; collision errors over five λ probes decreased from 6.8e−5 at d=.01 to 1.4e−8 at d=.0001. These samples supplement rather than establish the analytical claims.
residual_risks: No uniform finite-part expansion at λ=±1 is asserted; singular points and support endpoints have zero probability.

value.rationale: Separating the centers by this symmetry-preserving displacement poses a natural distribution question even after the coincident-center law is known. The global piecewise law specifies how one logarithmic density peak is replaced by two, with exact constants and a uniform finite crossover profile on their separation scale. This identifies the geometry from the distance law and provides an explicit benchmark for changes of radius or placement. The claim does not depend for its value on elementary identifiability by itself or on a supposedly new elliptic-integral expansion.
residual_risks: The exact solvability and profile have only been established in this one perpendicular, equal-radius displacement family.
